newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end a shade lower in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end a shade lower in slack trade.

text.p: Swiss share prices ended on a weaker note in slack trade and light volume as investors grew cautious given the high level of indices and a new closing high on Tuesday.
"People are reluctant to act as long as the market is that high up," a dealer said, adding a futures correction may trigger a year-end rally.
U.S. PPI data did not have much of an impact. Many transactions were derivatives-linked in light of the expiry of Swiss options and futures on Friday, a trader noted.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 4.1 points, or 0.11 percent, to 3,825.7 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 1.75 points at 2,443.97 points.
Industrials were buoyed by the firming tendency in the U.S. dollar and by the record level of the German bourse, which has a big share of cyclical stocks.
Actively-traded Roche certificates closed five francs higher at 9,735, while Ciba and Sandoz were slightly weaker.
Holderbank stood out with an gain of two percent to 912. Dealers said the stock had reached a level which triggered buys.
ABB profited from a steady flow of international orders, a trader noted. The stock rose 10 francs to 1,610.
Alusuisse jumped one percent to 976 francs. UBS had made derivatives-related purchases in the stock, a dealer noted.

Insurer Winterthur was flat at 764. The company said it would take over the remaining business of subsidiary Neuenburger and slash 150 jobs out of around 800 at Neuenburger. A dealer said the move did not come as a surprise.
Banks and insurers were mixed. UBS bearers fell siven francs to 1,242 while CS Holding and SBC were up. Insurer Baloise soared 55 francs to 2,775 on renewed takeover rumours.
As in the past few days, trade on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was heavily influenced by Friday's Soffex expiry. But overall activity was lethargic, dealers said.

Numerous futures and options have been rolled over, and roll-over transactions have probably been concluded by now, one trader noted. The open interest was at 13,000 contracts, which was considered relatively low two days ahead of the expiry.
10,486 SMI futures contracts were traded, of which roughly 6,700 were November contracts and around 3,600 were December contracts. Options volumes reached to 97,108 contracts.
